title: Tests repo: plant-products m0/m2 coverage — dashboard, import-type entry filter, hub skeleton, origin, purpose
recipe: No recipe. METHODS at this increment:
- `toNotificationDashboard()` — open the plant dashboard, wait for its heading
- `startNotification()` — dashboard → create → land on the IMPORT-TYPE filter → capture the journey id from the URL → pick the CHED-PP certificate type → continue → land on the HUB. Returns the journey id and records it on the shared `JourneyContext`. NOTE THE DIFFERENCE from live-animals, whose `startNotification()` continues into `originOfImport` before opening the overview (`journey.ts:35-39`): the plant flow lands on the hub, because §2.3's `start` section is `[dashboardPage, importTypePage]` and the hub is the spine. Do not transpose the live-animals sequencing.
- `answerOrigin(options)` — hub → spoke 1 → fill both country answers (+ optional internal reference) → save → back on the hub
- `answerPurpose(options)` — hub → spoke 2 → pick a reason → save → back on the hub

Each fill/save pair stays split (`fillX` / `saveX` / `answerX`) exactly as the live-animals flow does, so a validation spec can fill without saving and a happy-path spec can call the one-liner.

NEW AND LOAD-BEARING — this is the spec that proves per-set request isolation from the outside.

CASES:
1. A FRESH deep link (new browser context, no session) to a post-filter plant page — e.g. `/plant-products/notifications/{ref}/about-the-consignment` — redirects to the plant IMPORT-TYPE filter, not to the hub and not to live-animals.
2. It does NOT run the live-animals guard: the redirect target is under `/plant-products`, never `/live-animals` and never `/`.
3. The mirror case: a fresh deep link to a live-animals page still redirects to the LIVE-ANIMALS filter under `/live-animals`. Both halves in one spec, because the whole risk here is cross-talk.

WHY IT MATTERS: FD-15 resolves the set by ROUTE OWNERSHIP (a realm-scoped `onPreAuth` per gateway), and the plant entry guard builds its journey prefix from `setBase()` per request while `request.path` INCLUDES the mount prefix (§4.6 A row 6). Getting that wrong silently DISABLES the deep-link guard — the page renders, nothing errors, and only a spec that deep-links from a cold context notices. The frontend's own specs run one set on stubs; this is the first place both guards exist at once.

notes:
THE TESTS REPO IS A SEPARATE GIT REPO — own remote, own branch (`spike/trace-to-requirements`), own CI, own package.json. There is no frontend `test:features` here. Verbatim scripts: "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"; "lint": "eslint ."; "format:check": "prettier --check '**/*.{ts,js,mjs,md,json,yml,yaml}'"; "test": "npm run _assert_stack && npm run _clean && npm run database:reseed && npm run _test_e2e"; "test:local": "npm run test:integration"; "test:a11y": "npm run _clean_and_test -- --grep '@a11y'"; plus `test:plant-products` from pp-060.

WHAT THIS REPO ADDS OVER THE FRONTEND'S OWN SPECS: the frontend's in-repo `*.e2e.spec.js` run against a self-hosted server on the records STUB. These run the same journeys against the REAL workspace stack — real backend, real Mongo, real OIDC. Only the second proves a set actually works (§10 preamble). So every spec here should assert something the stub cannot prove: persisted codes, draft resume across a real save, dashboard scoping, cross-set isolation.

WHY THE ENTRY-GUARD SPEC IS THE MOST VALUABLE FILE IN THIS INCREMENT: co-residency puts two entry guards in one process, each realm-scoped by FD-15. Under a mount prefix `request.path` includes the prefix, so a guard whose journey prefix was captured at module load (or built without `setBase()`) silently stops matching — the page renders, nothing throws, and the deep-link protection is simply gone. No unit test in the frontend catches it because each in-repo suite composes one set. A cold-context deep link from outside is the only proof.

DO NOT SHARE PAGE OBJECTS ACROSS SETS. §10.2's ruling: the URL layer is parameterised, everything above it is cloned. Two files named `import-type-page.ts` under different set dirs is the intended outcome, not duplication to be refactored away — the plant page has different copy, different options and a different next page.

DEPENDS ON pp-020 (the frontend hub increment) because these specs walk to and from the hub. If pp-020 has not landed, the hub is not there to return to and every `answerX` fails at its last step.

ROLLBACK: `git stash push -u`, never `reset --hard` + `clean -fd`.
